title: Delta materializer + adaptive read-through cache for tenant aggregation queries
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Problem: Several customer dashboards experience high 95th/99th percentile latencies for heavy aggregation queries over recent time windows. Root causes include repeated full-window scans from the analytics OLAP layer, expensive grouping on high-cardinality dimensions, and cache eviction churn across tenants during bursts. Goal: reduce tail latency and read amplification for recent-window dashboard queries (last 1h, 24h) while preserving near-real-time freshness and keeping cost per query within target SLOs.
proposal_summary: Introduce a delta materializer that incrementally maintains tenant-scoped micro-rollups for recent windows and a tenant-tier aware read-through cache. The materializer consumes the existing analytics event stream to maintain small, append-only delta shards per tenant and time-epoch. Queries for recent windows first consult the materialized delta + sketch indexes to produce fast, approximate responses; exact aggregates are obtained by applying a small historical merge if needed. The read-through cache uses epoch fingerprints to maintain consistency and applies an adaptive eviction policy weighted by tenant SLA tier and access heat. Hedging: split long-running queries into a fast-path (materialized + sketch) and a backfill path; return fast-path result immediately with a metadata flag and update via websocket/stream when backfill completes.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile dashboard aggregator latency reduced by >= 40% for top-200 tenants in canary
Query amplification (average scanned rows per query) reduced by >= 60% for recent-window queries
Cache hit rate >= 75% for top-100 active dashboards during burst scenarios
No customer-facing data inconsistency reported in canary; epoch fingerprint mismatches audited
Rollback plan documented and validated in staging; canary rollback completes within 15 minutes
implementation_plan: Spike (2w): prototype delta shard format, epoch fingerprinting, and ingestion consumer. Validate storage footprint and update latency.
Prototype (3w): implement read-path that composes delta shards + historical micro-rollups; add tenant sketch index for cardinality reduction.
Canary (2w): route 10% traffic for top-5 tenants; collect SLOs and compare against baseline dashboards.
Rollout (3w): incrementally expand tenant coverage by tier; enable adaptive eviction and hedging policies in runtime configs.
Post-mortem & optimization (2w): tune thresholds, bake operational runbooks, and add observability panels
migration_notes: Backfill historical micro-rollups for the last 7 days will run offline and will be throttled to avoid pipeline pressure. New delta shard schema is backward-compatible for read services; implement a feature flag to switch reads to the materialized path. Coordinate with data-platform to enable event-stream consumer group and verify offsets.
observability: New dashboards: delta-shard-lag, delta-application-latency, tenant-cache-hit-rate, sketch-estimate-error. Add tracing spans for materializer apply and read-merge path. Create alert: delta_shard_lag > 60s for > 5 minutes.
rollback_plan: Toggle feature flag to route reads back to existing OLAP path; stop delta consumer; purge cache entries created by materialized path. Validate via canary queries and synthetic dashboards before full rollback.
progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Spike started. Prototype delta shard schema defined; initial consumer reads from event-stream and writes delta blobs to S3-like store. Estimated shard size ~ 120KB per tenant-hour based on sample workload.

2026-03-04: Prototype read-path returns composed results within 60-120ms for sample tenant; integration test added. Noted worst-case merge when historical micro-rollup absent; exploring on-demand micro-rollup generation.

2026-03-09: Review with PM and Data Platform. PM requested opt-in tenant whitelist for canary. Data Platform requested rate limits on backfill. Security flagged KMS usage for persisted deltas — added to plan.
2026-03-12: Canary infra prepared; canary config and PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rdfy/pull/4680. Preparing rollout checklist and runbook.
comments: Lena Park (assignee) 2026-03-05: Decided to use Murmur3 epoch fingerprinting for low-cost change detection. We'll store epoch metadata with each delta blob.
Arun Patel (PM) 2026-03-07: Make sure dashboard UX receives a metadata flag for 'partial' responses so frontend can render loading shimmer correctly. Follow-up: design to add 'staleness' tooltip.
Security Review 2026-03-10: Storage of tenant deltas must be encrypted with customer KMS when in Private deployments. Added requirement to technical design.
Sophie Nguyen (Data Platform) 2026-03-11: Backfill window will need throttled workers. We'll provide a dedicated backfill queue and OOM safeguards.
